icons.name: Arched-lid chest
icons.audit_note: Reviewed arched lid and pale panels. Project explicitly identifies this as a different-object stand-in; not a verified Treasury find or exact ancient chest.

icons.name: Anubis shrine
icons.audit_note: Rejected seated jackal and unsuccessful first edit; regenerated from GEM photograph with reclining body, extended forelegs and carrying poles.

icons.name: Outermost burial shrine
icons.audit_status: Reconstruction reference — not independent historical verification
icons.audit_note: Replaced open box with closed broad double-door enclosure, cornice, bolts and repeating panels. Fine blue faience colors are muted at this scale.

icons.name: Second burial shrine
icons.audit_status: Reconstruction reference — not independent historical verification
icons.audit_note: Matched the project’s reconstruction reference: broad double doors, standing figures, low cornice and bolts. Fine inscriptions are not verified.

icons.name: Third burial shrine
icons.audit_status: Reconstruction reference — not independent historical verification
icons.audit_note: Removed invented pyramid roof; matched the project’s reconstruction reference for the low cornice and double doors.

icons.name: Innermost burial shrine
icons.audit_status: Reconstruction reference — not independent historical verification
icons.audit_note: Replaced arched-lid treasure chest with the upright double-door shrine and winged protective figure in the reconstruction reference.

icons.name: Canopic shrine
icons.audit_status: Reconstruction reference — not independent historical verification
icons.audit_note: Replaced fabricated exposed coffinette arrangement with shrine posts, cobra frieze and protective goddess. This is an exterior shrine icon, not a diagram of its internal chest.

icons.name: Chariot
icons.audit_note: Reviewed two-wheel chariot form with pole and open body. Wheel-spoke count, decoration and exact chariot identity remain illustrative.

icons.name: Anthropoid coffin
icons.audit_note: Reviewed anthropoid outline as a generic modern replica icon. Do not identify this stylized image as a fourth original coffin or assign it a Carter number.

icons.name: Crook and flail
icons.audit_note: Removed second hooked handle. One hooked crook and one straight flail with three strands; stray left-side tassel removed by guarded exact pixel edits. Type-level teaching icon.

icons.name: Iron dagger and gold sheath
icons.audit_note: Changed the incorrectly green pommel to pale rock crystal. Iron blade and separate gold sheath retained. Decoration is illustrative, not an exact tracing.

icons.name: Royal diadem
icons.audit_note: Replaced generic band with GEM photograph-based cobra/vulture insignia and hanging appendages. The museum photo crops the ends of some ribbons; they are not independently restored.

icons.name: Ceremonial fan
icons.audit_note: Reviewed feather-fan type and handle. Full feathers are a reconstruction; exact feather count, ornament and surviving condition are not verified against a specific original.

icons.name: Cow-headed funerary couch
icons.audit_note: Reviewed intended cow-headed couch type and horned sun disks. Broad form and display base remain a teaching reconstruction, not a verified copy of Carter 73.

icons.name: Funerary couch
icons.audit_note: Reviewed lion-couch type. Source project already notes problems with the older couch reconstruction; leg count and ornament are not independently verified. Keep labeled study reconstruction.

icons.name: Guardian with khat headdress
icons.audit_status: Reconstruction reference — not independent historical verification
icons.audit_note: Replaced nemes-like striped headwear with the smooth khat reference; restored black body, long gold kilt, staff and mace.

icons.name: Guardian with nemes headcloth
icons.audit_status: Reconstruction reference — not independent historical verification
icons.audit_note: Replaced bright blue ornament and short kilt with the reference’s restrained black-and-gold finish, long kilt and regalia.

icons.name: Ivory headrest with Shu and lions
icons.audit_note: Removed invented blue and gold ornament and human-faced lions; used the museum photograph of the ivory crescent, Shu and reclining lions.

icons.name: Dark-blue faience headrest
icons.audit_note: Added missing separate 403b icon from the project’s reference photograph. Dark-blue glaze appears light/desaturated under the photograph’s lighting.

icons.name: Turquoise glass headrest
icons.audit_note: Added missing separate 403a icon from the project’s reference photograph. Surface colors and wear follow that image, not a measured material rendering.

icons.name: Table-shaped headrest cabinet
icons.audit_note: Added missing cabinet icon from museum reference: solid box, flat lid and table-like legs. Tiny inlay details simplified.

icons.name: Folding ivory headrest
icons.audit_status: Reconstruction reference — not independent historical verification
icons.audit_note: Added missing separate 403d icon using the project’s generated reference view; crossing supports and carved ends preserved. Reconstruction, not independent museum-photo verification.

icons.name: Innermost gold coffin
icons.audit_status: Reconstruction reference — not independent historical verification
icons.audit_note: Separate Carter 255 icon using the project’s reconstruction front: slender gold metal coffin, gold headcloth, crossed arms and closed foot end.

icons.name: Calcite perfume vessel
icons.audit_note: Replaced generic amphora with Carter 210’s elaborate sculptural vessel and trellis pedestal. Monochrome archival source; small carved details remain simplified.

icons.name: Head emerging from a lotus
icons.audit_note: Replaced the broad open flower and invented hair with the source model’s elongated bald head, narrow lotus calyx, stem and round base.

icons.name: Wooden portrait bust
icons.audit_note: Removed invented striped nemes and jeweled collar; matched the source model’s tall crown and pale armless torso.

icons.name: Gold funerary mask
icons.audit_note: Checked mask type against the GEM color photograph: gold face, striped nemes, beard and broad collar. Retained stylized icon; tiny insignia and inlays are simplified.

icons.name: Middle coffin
icons.audit_status: Reconstruction reference — not independent historical verification
icons.audit_note: Separate Carter 254 icon; corrected muted first result to distinguish blue/gold headcloth and colorful feather inlay from the outer and inner coffins.

icons.name: Model boat, second example
icons.audit_note: Reviewed separate sailing-boat silhouette. Sail, mast and cabin are illustrative; no secure Carter number or exact source boat is established.

icons.name: Model boat
icons.audit_note: Reviewed hull, central cabin and steering-oar type. No secure Carter number for this AI comparison; exact boat identity and details remain unverified.

icons.name: Three nested coffins
icons.audit_note: Retained only as a simplified assembly icon. Individual outer, middle and inner coffins now have separate files; this diagram is not a measured nesting/clearance model.

icons.name: Outermost coffin
icons.audit_status: Reconstruction reference — not independent historical verification
icons.audit_note: Separate Carter 253 icon using the project’s reconstruction front: broad gilded-wood body, gold headcloth and restrained carving. Not blue-striped like the middle coffin.

icons.name: Painted wooden chest
icons.audit_note: Replaced generic treasure chest with archival photograph’s broad chest and painted scene panels; cleaned photographic backdrop. Monochrome source; original color not established from this image.

icons.name: Scarab pectoral, alternate
icons.audit_note: Recomposed necklace completely within transparent margins. Exact ancient pectoral match unverified; retain as an explicitly illustrative alternate design.

icons.name: Sandals
icons.audit_note: Reviewed pair and recognizable sandal type. Straps, sole decoration and precise correspondence to Tutankhamun’s gold funerary sandals remain unverified.

icons.name: Scarab bracelet
icons.audit_note: Added omitted bracelet artwork. Visually checked the actual Marius Ciulei source model: raised dark-blue scarab atop circular gold hinged bangle with red, ivory and turquoise shoulder inlays. PixelLab illustration preserves those identifying features; exact ancient identity and findspot remain unverified.

icons.name: Winged scarab pectoral
icons.audit_note: Changed outstretched fantasy wings to the source model’s upward-curving rounded wings and central turquoise scarab. The source model itself is an artistic reconstruction with no secure ancient catalog match.

icons.name: Senet board and pieces
icons.audit_note: Replaced uncountable generated grid with exact PixelLab workbench drawing: 30 cells in 3 rows of 10; cone and spool pieces. Generic teaching board, not a facsimile of Carter 345.

icons.name: Royal shabti with blue crown
icons.audit_note: Reviewed mummiform silhouette, crossed arms and blue crown. Kept as royal type illustration; exact ancient object, surface colors and inscription unverified.

icons.name: Royal shabti with nemes headcloth
icons.audit_note: Removed separate living-person legs and short skirt; corrected lower half to continuous mummiform body. Royal type illustration; exact ancient object and inscription unverified.

icons.name: Shawabti of Horudja, comparison
icons.audit_note: Removed bright emerald and gold trim; matched source model’s pale gray-green narrow figure. Different ancient owner, not a Tutankhamun find.

icons.name: Shawabti of Nedjem, comparison
icons.audit_note: Matched source model’s dark worn figure and crossed arms; removed invented bright paint and oversized projecting tools. Different ancient owner, not a Tutankhamun find.

icons.name: Shawabti of Nesi-qa-Shu, comparison
icons.audit_note: Removed cream bandages and royal headcloth; matched source model’s worn green surface and plain figure. Different ancient owner, not a Tutankhamun find.

icons.name: Shawabti of Psamtik, comparison
icons.audit_note: Replaced invented royal ornament with source model’s muted green faience and narrow plain figure. Different ancient owner, not a Tutankhamun find.

icons.name: Shawabti of Ramose, comparison
icons.audit_note: Matched cream paint, dark wig, crossed hands and vertical markings of the credited model. Different ancient owner, not a Tutankhamun find.

icons.name: Openwork ceremonial shield
icons.audit_note: Reviewed arch-top, flat-base openwork silhouette. Royal and animal motifs remain illustrative; no secure ancient catalog match established.

icons.name: Ceremonial shield
icons.audit_note: Corrected round shield to tall arch-top, flat-base form and removed giant pharaoh face. Central figure/lion ornament remains illustrative; no secure ancient catalog match.

icons.name: Golden throne
icons.audit_note: Replaced the invented large face on the back with a reference-based king-and-queen scene; restored open frame, thin legs and separate footstool.

icons.name: Decorated throwing sticks
icons.audit_note: Replaced straight thin staffs with broad curved throwing sticks. Archival comparison is Carter 54d/e; exact identity of the game’s AI mesh remains unverified. Monochrome source.
